text: Mitosis [Gr. mitoV , a thread]: Ger. Mitose ; Fr. mitose ; Ital. mitosi . The indirect mode of nuclear division, to which the term karyokinesis is also applied. The chromatin of the nucleus forms a thread, which breaks up into a number of separate CHROMOSOMES (q.v.); these become split each into two halves, which travel to the opposite poles of the achromatic spindle (amphiaster), where they become reconstituted into the two daughter nuclei. Mitosis is the ordinary mode of nuclear division, and is found, with but little variation, in the cell division of the Protozoa and Metazoa, and of plants also. Cf. CELL THEORY (also for literature), AMITOSIS, and NUCLEUS. ( E.S.G. )
